checks.quote:
Some crops can tolerate drought because they are able to
resist a shortage of water, i.e. they are said to be drought-resistant. This is
because either:
they can stop
growing when water is unavailable by becoming dormant. When rain occurs they
resume growing and developing as though nothing had happened; or
they have deep rooting
systems, such as pigeon pea, and can absorb water from deep within the soil.
This is important where occasional rainstorms wet the soil to great depth
followed by long dry periods.
